result.title: Two-Stage Post-Training for Flow-Based Embodied Foundation Models
result.summary: Large-scale pretraining provides embodied models with general capabilities, but reliable task execution still requires post training. In multitask settings, supervised fine-tuning (SFT) faces distribution mismatch between training and deployment, whereas reinforcement learning (RL) is limited by sparse rewards and uneven learning progress across tasks. Multi-teacher on policy distillation (MOPD) consolidates expert capabilities through dense supervision on the model's own trajectories, but achieving performance beyond the teachers remains challenging. We propose a two-stage post training framework for flow-based embodied models, constructing distillation objectives from the velocity regression formulation of conditional flow matching. Stage 1 efficiently consolidates expert capabilities through MOPD. Stage 2 combines RL with teacher distillation that weights velocity errors according to the sampling noise, where distillation is restricted to failed trajectories to supplement sparse rewards with dense guidance without directly constraining successful behaviors. Experiments across multiple models and benchmarks show that the framework outperforms joint SFT and exceeds the corresponding teachers' aggregate success rates. Sample efficiency comparisons show higher success rates than direct RL with fewer environment interactions.

AI.brief_summary: 面向 flow-based 具身基础模型提出两阶段后训练框架：第一阶段用多教师 on-policy 蒸馏整合专家能力，第二阶段在 RL 中仅对失败轨迹施加按采样噪声加权速度误差的教师蒸馏，以密集指导补足稀疏奖励，实验显示优于联合 SFT 且交互更少。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「仅对失败轨迹蒸馏、按噪声加权误差」的选择性监督思路，可能为 LVR 轨迹训练中的贡献分配与稀疏反馈下的密集监督提供可核查线索，但该工作在机器人控制域，未涉及视觉 latent 状态表示。
